q: With SSR, once the HTML has arrived and the button is on screen, the button always works right away.
why: No. The HTML is only a picture until the JavaScript has loaded and React has hydrated it. Early taps can do nothing.

q: In ISR, what does the visitor who triggers the background rebuild see?
options: A loading spinner until the new page is ready
The new page, because the rebuild is instant
why: ISR serves the saved copy at once and rebuilds in the background. Nobody waits for the rebuild. This is stale while revalidate.

q: Which of these make a part of a Next.js 16 page dynamic, so it needs Suspense or caching?
options: A pure calculation with no request data
why: Request data (cookies, headers, searchParams) and uncached database or API calls need request time. Pure calculations finish at build time and go into the static shell.

q: What does a <Suspense> boundary decide on a Next.js 16 page?
options: What is in the static shell and what streams in later
Which components run in the browser
How long data stays in the cache
Which pages are built at deploy time
why: Everything outside Suspense is the shell and is sent first. The fallback sits in the shell. The content inside streams in when its data is ready.

q: Put the steps of a first page load in order.
items: The browser asks the server for the page
The server sends the shell HTML
The browser shows the page, but it is not clickable
why: Seeing the page comes before using it. Hydration is the last step, and only then do clicks work.

q: Which Next.js function lists the dynamic addresses (like /blog/[slug]) that should be built at build time?
why: generateStaticParams returns the list of params to prebuild. Other params can be built on the first visit.
